title: L6 Extended Capstone: Plugin Framework
story: You've mastered interfaces, modules, generics, and testing. Now build something that ties them all together: a mini plugin framework. Define a plugin interface, create multiple plugin implementations, organize them in modules, and test them all. This is real architecture in miniature.
why: Building a plugin framework synthesizes all L6 concepts into a single program: interfaces define contracts, modules organize code, generics provide flexibility, tests ensure correctness.
analogy: A music studio has a rack of effects processors — compressor, reverb, delay, EQ. Each effect is a plugin implementing the 'AudioEffect' interface. You can swap them, chain them, bypass them — the rack (plugin manager) doesn't care about the internals, only that each plugin handles `process(audio)`.
try_it: Add `ShoutPlugin` (all caps), `WhisperPlugin` (all lowercase), and `CountPlugin` (returns character count as string). Add a `run_one` function that runs a specific plugin by index. Write a test that verifies each plugin's output.
tips: The Plugin interface is the contract — every plugin must implement name() and execute()
Keep the plugin manager generic so it works with any plugin type
This pattern scales: you could load plugins dynamically, add priority ordering, etc.
common_mistakes: Trying to store different plugin types in the same Vec — they must be the same T
Forgetting to constrain T: Plugin on the Manager type and all its methods
Making plugins do too much — each should do one transformation well
